full_judgment:
Md Badruzzaman J: Since common question of facts and law are involved in the aforesaid criminal miscellaneous cases those have been heard together and now are being disposed of by this common judgment. 

 2. Relevant facts, for the purpose of disposal of these rules, are that, opposite party No.2 as complainant filed five complaint cases against the accused-petitioner and two others under sections 138/140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 before the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. In said complaint cases the accused-petitioner has been impleaded as accused No.2 being the Managing Director of accused No.1, Chandradeep Builders & Developers Limited and accused No.3 is the Chairman of accused No.1. Common case as extracted from the complaints is that the accused-petitioner as the Managing Director and accused No.2 as the Chairman of accused No.1, company jointly issued five separate cheques from the account of accused No.1 in favour of the complainant being cheques dated 28-2-2015 for an amount of Taka 10,00,000; dated 8-3-2015 for an amount of Taka 10,00,000; dated 29-3-2015 for an amount of Taka 10,00,000; dated 15-4-2015 for an amount of Taka 10,00,000; and dated 24-4-2015 for an amount of Taka 11,00,000 in due course, those cheques were placed for encasement in his account but all cheques were dishonored for insufficiency of fund and after complying all legal requirements, opposite party No. 2 filed five separate CR cases against the accused-petitioner and two others, as stated above. Being received the process of the cases, accused-petitioner voluntarily surrendered before the learned Magistrate and obtained bail and being ready, the cases were transferred to the learned Special Joint Sessions Judge and Paribash Adalat, Dhaka for trial and renumbered as metro sessions cases being Metro Sessions Cases No. 12412 of 2015, 110 of 2015, 12413 of 2015, 4629 of 2015 and 12415 of 2015 and learned Judge, after hearing both the parties, framed charge against the accused-petitioner and another the Chairman of the company section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 and fixed for evidence. 

 3. Thereafter, the accused-petitioner has come up with five separate applications under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceedings of said five cases and obtained rules in the following terms: 

 4. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 35541 of 2017 rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceeding of Metro Sessions Case No. 12412 of 2015 arising out of CR Case No. 104 of 2015 under sections 138/140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before the learned Special Joint Sessions Judge and Poribesh Adalat, Dhaka, should not be quashed. 

 5. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 39063 of 2017 Rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Metro Sessions Case No. 12414 of 2015 arising out of CR Case No. 110 of 2015 (Shahabagh Tahana) under sections 138/140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before the learned Special Joint Sessions Judge and Poribesh Adalat, Dhaka, should not be quashed. 

 6. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 39064 of 2017 rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Metro Sessions Case No.12413 of 2015 arising out of CR Case No. 108 of 2015 (Shahabagh Tahana) under sections 138/140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before the learned Special Joint Sessions Judge and Poribesh Adalat, Dhaka, should not be quashed. 

 7. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 39065 of 2017 rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Metro Sessions Case No. 4629 of 2016 arising out of CR Case No. 2439 of 2016 (Motijheel Tahana) under sections 138/140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before the learned Special Joint Sessions Judge and Poribesh Adalat, Dhaka, should not be quashed. 

 8. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 39066 of 2017 rule was issued calling upon the opposite-parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Metro Sessions Case No.12415 of 2015 arising out of CR Case No. 111 of 2015 (Shahabagh Tahana) under sections 138/140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before the learned Special Joint Sessions Judge and Poribesh Adalat, Dhaka, should not be quashed. 

 9. At the time of issuance of Rules, another Division of this Court vides ad-interim orders passed on different dates stayed further proceedings of the aforesaid metro sessions cases which are still continuing. 

 10. It is the case of the accused-petitioner that admittedly, the accused-petitioner is Managing Director of the developer company (accused No.1) and complaint opposite party No. 2 is the land owner and an agreement has been signed and executed between the company and the land owner for construction 

 of multi-storied commercial building on the disputed land and as per terms of the agreement, the company agreed to pay the land owner as advance money against the property to be developed by the company and the complainant-land owner had agreed to handover the land to the company and as per terms of the contract, the company gave seven cheques including the disputed cheques in which the accused-petitioner as the Managing Director and accused No.3 as the Chairman of the company are joint signatories. After obtaining cheques from the accused-petitioner, the land owner encashed two cheques amounting to total Taka 20,00,000 and thereafter, it has been detected that before signing of the agreement, the land owner transferred the land to be developed to his sons by way of gift and after such detection about transfer, the accused-petitioner instructed the bank for stop payment against five cheques in question and accordingly, the said cheques have been dishonored when the same were placed for encashment. After filing the CR cases for dishonor of cheques, opposite party No.2 filed Title Suit No. 13 of 2016 before the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka for declarations that the registered development agreement as well as power-of-attorney dated 9-2-2015 are ineffective and not binding upon him and in the plaint, opposite party No. 2 specifically admitted that the cheques have been issued against development agreement and that the agreement executed between the parties has not been acted upon. 

 13. We have perused the applications, complaint petitions, plaint of title suit and other documents available on record. From the submissions made by learned Advocate for the accused-petitioner, it appears that his whole case depends on the defense materials for quashing the proceedings. 

 16. In exercising inherent jurisdiction under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure the defense materials, which need to be proved upon trial by adducing evidence, cannot be looked into and accepted for quashing a criminal proceeding. This power also cannot be exercised when prima facie case has been disclosed and cognizance taken. But there is no doubt that in exercise of the powers under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure the High Court has ample inherent powers to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice (Ref: 32 DLR 187). The expression "abuse of process" in section 561A means in effect anything done by the Court. Inherent power of the Court is extraordinary in its nature and is exercised ex debito justitiae, that is to say, for the purpose of doing justice that real and substantial justice for the administration of which the Courts of law exist. The inherent jurisdiction is attracted firstly, "to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order of the Code". Secondly, "to prevent abuse of the process of any Court" and lastly, "otherwise to secure ends of justice". [Ref: 32 DLR (AD) 1]. In the instant cases, though prima facie case has been disclosed in the complaint petitions, the inherent jurisdiction under second and last categories is attracted. Accordingly, we are of the view that further prolongation of the proceedings would amount to harassment to the accused-petitioner and abuse of the process of the Court and hence, liable to be quashed to secure ends of justice. 

 18. In the result, the rules are made absolute. The proceedings of Metro Sessions Case No. 12412 of 2015, Metro Sessions Case No. 110 of 2015, Metro Sessions Case No.12413 of 2015, Metro Sessions Case No. 4629 of 2016 and Metro Sessions Case No.12415 of 2015, under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, now pending before Special Joint Sessions Judge and Paribash Adalat, Dhaka are hereby quashed.
